column3: NASB follows the critical text with “Gerasenes.”
NASB renders “fell on his knees” as “bowed down.”
NASB renders “What to me and to You” as “What business do we have with each other” and “adjure” as “implore.”
NASB renders the imperfect “was saying” as “had been saying.”
NASB follows the critical text; “Legion is my name” is rendered “My name is Legion.”
NASB follows the critical text with “The demons” (no “all”).
NASB follows the critical text; it supplies “the people.”
NASB puts “legion” in quotation marks and adds “the very man.”
NASB renders “be with Him” as “accompany Him.”
NASB follows the critical text; “to your own” is rendered “to your people,” and it adds “how.”
NASB adds “and so He stayed”; “beside the sea” is “by the seashore.”
NASB renders “synagogue rulers” as “synagogue officials” and has no “behold,” like the critical text.
“Is at the end” is rendered “is at the point of death”; NASB adds “please” and renders “be saved” as “get well.”
“She was saying” is rendered “she thought”; “be saved” is “get well.”
